question: Should OpenClaw core own a persisted publisher-follow and signed-feed trust lifecycle now, or should this remain outside core until the feed RFC and plugin/ClawHub ownership boundary are explicitly approved?
rationale: The patch introduces a new CLI, persistent shared-state records, remote trust-profile resolution, and follow lifecycle policy; tests can validate mechanics but cannot decide the permanent core product boundary.

options.title: Pause for core/RFC sponsorship
options.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until an owner explicitly confirms the core trust and lifecycle boundary; then require upgrade and live behavior proof.

options.title: Move the lifecycle outside core
options.body: Route publisher following to a plugin or ClawHub-owned package if existing plugin/config seams can own the feature without a new core trust surface.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core slice
options.body: Approve only a documented, upgrade-proven minimal core contract and defer gateway/UI scheduling and broader lifecycle policy to later work.

recommendation.title: Pause for core/RFC sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until an owner explicitly confirms the core trust and lifecycle boundary; then require upgrade and live behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only evidence-backed contributor spanning the proposed protocol, verifier, transport, state, and gateway slices; a repository owner should make the final product decision.
